correctness.rationale: On arbitrary nonempty finite one-agent Kripke frames with fixed valuation and repeated hedged contraction by Diamond p, define P=V(p), A_t={w:S_t(w) meets P}, N_t=W\A_t. Actual update is S_{t+1}(w)=S_t(w) union N_t iff S_t(w) subset A_t. Arrow-addition implies A_t increases. If A_{t+1}=A_t, any row either already meets N_t or receives all N_t; consequently no row is eligible after t+1 and the next update is stationary. Counting strict growth stages plus at most one final nongrowing stage, separately covering A0 empty and P empty, proves first stationary stage <=n. Directed path i->i+1 with P={0} changes exactly one new row at each of n stages, then fixes. Independent fresh bitmask enumeration of all valuations and relations for n=1,2,3 (4+64+4096 cases) and sharp-path checks n=4,5,10,30 match. Original checker exhausts n<=4 but its claimed count was not assumed as proof. No seriality/reflexivity assumed.
